skyNote: The recording's background is the painting as a flat picture bent by a cubic map (not an equirectangular sky seen through the lens: that model has no solution, every earlier fit failed on it). The map takes the recording's pixel in the 1920 by 864 frame, x = (px - 960) / 960 and y = (py - 432) / 432, to the picture's pixel in 1774 by 887: the first 10 numbers are the x coefficients, the next 10 the y coefficients, terms [1, x, y, x2, xy, y2, x3, x2y, xy2, y3]. Matched with SIFT on five frames of horizontal.mkv (248 inliers), then refined three times by optical flow between the warped picture and the recording on the pixels where the character is absent (1262 samples; median residual 1.2 px of 1920, 90th percentile 13 px), pulled to the best affine map where nothing matched. `sky` is the rest camera's rotation transposed (her space to the camera). See round7-CAM-landscape.md

landscape.note: horizontal.mkv: ONE static camera for idle, pose and both transitions (the recording's background never moves). Position = the game's camera position (0, 1.1053, 0.9545 in her space), vertical field of view 60 degrees over the whole 2.222 frame, optical axis in the middle, rotation (rotvec in her space) [-0.1065, -0.023, -0.2586]: fitted by 10 landmarks (eyes, claw tips, wrist), rms 11 px of 1920, see round7-CAM-landscape.md

portrait.note: vertical.mkv shares horizontal.mkv's one static camera (the backgrounds agree), so the portrait camera is the landscape camera. A portrait window is a crop of the recording's frame: [fx, fy, h] = the window's middle as a share of the frame's width and height, and its height as a share of the frame's height (see round7-CAM-portrait.md). vertical.mkv's pose is another clip (the left hand's kiss), not city_interaction_R_loop.
